label: MSE is fine to use for classification
description:
MSE on classification logits or probabilities looks reasonable but has two failure modes. First, the gradient of MSE composed with sigmoid (or softmax) saturates: when the prediction is far from the target, the sigmoid gradient is tiny, so the loss gradient w.r.t. the logits is also tiny, and learning slows to a crawl. Cross-entropy avoids this by exactly cancelling the sigmoid/softmax derivative — gradient w.r.t. logits is just (predicted − target).

Second, MSE on one-hot targets does not produce calibrated probabilities; it pushes outputs toward 0 and 1 regardless of class confidence. For Bernoulli/Categorical likelihoods, cross-entropy is the maximum-likelihood loss; MSE is not.
probeQuestions: If you put MSE on top of a sigmoid output and the model predicts 0.99 when the label is 0, what's the gradient w.r.t. the logit?
Why does cross-entropy produce a clean (predicted - target) gradient at the logit level?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner is using MSE for a classification head. Walk through: MSE composed with sigmoid/softmax saturates at the extremes — the sigmoid derivative kills the gradient. Show that cross-entropy gives gradient (p - y) at the logit. Tie to MLE for Bernoulli/Categorical likelihoods. Ask the saturation probe first.
